topic: Round two of the external sk-code surface priority research. Round one (research/research.md in this spec folder, findings F1-F33, recommendations R1-R5, rejected ideas X1-X9, phases P1-P4) found that the one order source is sk-code hub-router.json routerPolicy.tieBreak; a user's own surface outranks the native sk-code-opencode if it is inserted ahead of opencode (R1); stack-agnostic tooling must stop naming the obsidian and webflow examples (R2); deleting the examples must become a documented, verified path including the re-mint and authored copy (R3); the two surfaces must be marked as examples (R4); R5 (opencode generic keywords) stays as is by operator ruling. Background: sk-code-obsidian and sk-code-webflow are the operator's personal example surfaces; an external user deletes them and adds their own surface, which must outrank sk-code-opencode. sk-code-review, sk-code-quality and shared/ are stack-agnostic. Round two goes deeper, with path:line or command evidence: (1) F10, ROUTER.md stack-agnostic intents (debugging, performance, deployment, accessibility, implementation) load mostly or only Webflow leaves, so after an external user deletes webflow those intents load almost nothing: what shared/ or opencode leaves could serve them, and a proposed R6; (2) F20, compiled-routing re-mint depends on the authored closure under specs/sk-doc/z_archive/019-skill-routing-refactor/, so a user who prunes specs/ cannot re-mint: cost and blast radius of fixing it versus documenting it, and R7 or a reasoned no; (3) F18, adding a surface by hand fails five doctor legs (3d-files, 6b, 5k-alias, 5k-packet, 5k-canary): does /create:skill-parent update --surfaces (.skilled/commands/create/skill-parent.md and its assets) perform those steps, observed in a throwaway full-tree copy; (4) stress-test R1-R4: exact edit text, every file each one touches (including the auto twin of create-skill-parent-confirm.yaml, both README tables, the sk-code README), what can still break, and whether each is the smallest correct fix under .skilled/repo-rules/prevent-overengineering.md; (5) anything round one missed: other hubs or tooling that assume sk-code's examples (benchmarks, playbooks, feature catalogs, advisor batteries and fixtures, Hermes and runtime mirrors, CI workflows under .github/, install guides, /doctor:update release-engine keep-local rules) and the end-to-end external-user flow (clone, delete examples, add own surface, run doctor, route a prompt); (6) challenge the rejected ideas X1-X9 once more and name new rejections. Every recommendation must pass .skilled/repo-rules/prevent-overengineering.md: name the cheaper move and why it fails. Number new findings from F34, new recommendations from R6 and new rejections from X10 only in the final synthesis; inside iterations use the finding-row format the preamble gives.
